evidence: Ter. Heaut. 2.3.114: tibi erunt parāta verba (Lewis & Short s.v. parō)
terms.comment: The participle of parāre, prepare. Of a person, “ready to” takes the infinitive or ad + acc.

evidence: Caes. BC 1.3: laudat promptōs (Lewis & Short s.v. prōmō)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “at hand, prepared, ready, quick, prompt”; it stresses willingness more than parātus does.

sources: Lewis & Short: paro · Lewis & Short: promo
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 69.
